Distinguishes packet labels from the native six-class dataset; 8,323/1,040/1,041 split counts match native validation.

Five distinct stored inputs shared between train/validation and six shared between train/test are disclosed; no independent-capture or new-holdout claim. Zero exact validation/test overlap is in the linked calibration guide/protocol/artifacts, not spoken in this chapter.
Describes the native JSON contract, 5 x 320 byte positions, normalization, 20 size values and 20 transformed intervals, token assembly and six logits.
Pinned model and runtime records support 400+20+20+3=443 tokens, width 256, four blocks and 1,870,080 total parameters.
The inherited claim that every embedding is learned was corrected to a numerical representation; size/interval value encodings are fixed sine/cosine, with learned position/modality components.
Separates reconstruction pretraining, labeled fine-tuning and frozen inference; introduces batches, epochs, gradients, optimizer updates and checkpoints.

Recorded short pretraining completes 132 updates across two epochs; epoch mean losses round to 9.51953 and 6.12702. It does not initialize the three principal fine-tunes or reproduce paper-scale pretraining.
Three seeds retain 120 epochs, 7,920 updates, batch 128 and derived maximum learning rate 0.001; validation selects checkpoints and the same fixed test split supplies final evaluation.
Explains repro/evaluate/predict/replay responsibilities, original source ownership and verified 103-file source inventory, configs/assets and run manifests.
New calibration is a positive scalar applied after model logits; native targets are discarded before forward. Fitting uses validation labels, and artifacts bind checkpoint/config/classes/runtime.
Raw predictions and scores remain available; no CSV-to-flow adapter, live capture or unlabeled accuracy is promised.
All original correct counts/accuracies, mean 86.65% and sample SD 4.00 percentage points match saved results; spread is not a confidence interval.

The baseline audit supports seven CUDA comparisons, complete-model one-step/strict-reload functionality on six synthetic fixtures and three fresh seed-0 runs retaining 1,041 classes with max FP16 difference 0.00390625.

Independently recomputed all paired test metrics for all three checkpoints; NLL/Brier/ECE improve for each, accuracy does not. Spoken means round correctly, with ECE converted from fractions to percentages.
Replay remains a saved seed-0 demonstration with no browser model execution. JSON row 635 appears as browser row 0636 and remains Other misclassified as RTSP Brute Force.
The optional prediction command uses a previously fitted calibration artifact and an illustrative threshold 0.90; missing/incompatible artifacts fail rather than silently falling back.

The 620 accepted/9 wrong to 893 accepted/37 wrong seed-0 comparison is exact. Accepted-set error uses accepted rows as denominator and is undefined for an empty accepted set. Calibration is not claimed to repair row 635.
The stale unqualified statement denying any calibration validation was corrected to lack of customer-traffic reliability and unknown-attack validation.
Retains three alternative routes: presentation, portable Git/Python checks, and checked Linux CUDA model execution with acquired assets.
Six hosted OS/Python combinations match the current workflow; successful portable checks do not establish Windows/macOS/CPU/NPU neural execution.

Actual CLI help accepts the demonstrated calibration and prediction options. Final displayed commands invoke the current v4 coverage verifier; historical v3 verification remains a separate supported command.
Retains root entry points, configuration, dependencies, ignored local assets, acquisition/build/profile/benchmark/export/calibration tools, tests/workflows and evidence relationships.
Explains synthetic Andrew voice rendering of Codex-authored text, retired course builders and separate historical versus current downloads.

Source promises a complete file guide; this review assesses that teaching intent only. Exact current tracked/untracked inventory and completed companion outputs require the separate final coverage/document checks.
Model-only batch-one latency rounds from 0.881265 ms, with 20 warmups and 100 measurements; capture, assembly, preprocessing, transfers and response are excluded.
SmartNIC/NPU division is future architecture; the strict graph-export probe failed at a custom causal-convolution CUDA operator. No deployed accelerator or CPU-model backend is claimed.

Final gaps preserve unreproduced paper accuracy/full pretraining, reused checkpoint-selection validation, already-seen test data, unknown independent customer reliability, live extraction, unknown attacks and operational policies.
The final 90-second practice and concise handoff retain the seven-question explanation without declaring the research/deployment gaps closed.
